claims.text: The selected high-entropy alloy becomes superconducting through conventional BCS electron–phonon pairing.
Greater configurational disorder enhances effective electron–phonon coupling in the dirty limit.
Greater configurational disorder favors an isotropic s-wave gap.
Greater configurational disorder produces robust low-temperature superconductivity.
The starting alloy has a simple crystalline structure such as BCC and random mixing of at least five elements.
A comparison alloy can be made with reduced configurational disorder while retaining a similar crystal structure.
Relevant superconducting transitions in this class occur below approximately 10 K.
Local chemical disorder consists of local atomic arrangements and site-to-site compositional variations.
X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy can quantify the relevant local chemical disorder.
Spectroscopic measurements of the Fermi-level density of states can quantify the proposed structural mediator.
High configurational entropy broadens the phonon spectrum.
High configurational entropy modifies the electronic density of states.
Disorder-induced changes to the phonon spectrum and density of states tune electron–phonon coupling strength.
Disorder scattering places the alloy in the dirty limit and thereby produces a conventional isotropic s-wave state.
The resulting superconducting state is robust against pressure variation.
The highly disordered alloy will have a transition temperature and lower and upper critical fields consistent with dirty-limit s-wave BCS superconductivity.
Reducing configurational disorder will alter, and likely lower, Tc relative to the highly disordered baseline.
Reducing configurational disorder will alter the lower or upper critical fields relative to the highly disordered baseline.
The proposed mechanism is limited to sufficiently high-entropy alloys with simple lattices and may fail when magnetism or strong electronic correlations dominate.
A lack of statistically significant disorder-dependent change in Tc, critical fields, or gap symmetry would undermine the proposed disorder-controlled mechanism.
